# dsh-opencode-patch layer.
#
# Adds one host plugin row that manages session affinity, OpenCode Zen gateway
# origin headers, free-tier compatibility, a models.dev-backed model catalog,
# and a live Go quota / session-spend meter.
#
# NOTE: `name` must equal this package's npm name (dsh-opencode-patch) —
# the host resolves row names to node_modules paths. `id` is the
# settings namespace and the plugin's own `name` export.
#
# Configuration (row `config`, all optional):
#
# Shown in the settings card (Settings -> Plugins -> OpenCode Patch). These are
# the decisions a user actually makes: behaviour toggles, plus the credential
# policy. See src/settings-fields.ts CARD_FIELDS.
#   injectUserAgent: boolean    restore OpenCode CLI User-Agent stripped by DSH adapter (default true).
#   injectOriginHeaders: bool   inject x-opencode-client (default true).
#   injectProject: boolean      attach active workspace project in x-opencode-project (default true).
#   enrichModels: boolean       merge the models.dev catalog into gateway model listings and DSH
#                               model discovery; off leaves both raw (default true).
#   injectCoreTools: boolean    auto-inject read & bash tool schemas on free models (default true).
#   usageEnabled: boolean       enable host-side OpenCode Go usage querying (default true).
#   keySource: string           which credential source wins: auto | request | configured (default 'auto').
#   readOpencodeStore: boolean  read the credential an OpenCode installation already holds, as the LAST
#                               resort after every declared one (default false).
#   endpoint: string            endpoint family: auto | modern | legacy (default 'auto', an alias of
#                               modern). modern = the per-protocol inference family; legacy = one base
#                               per plane.
#
# Config-only overrides — the card deliberately hides these, because each is a
# literal, a marker, or a reference whose default fits every documented setup.
# See src/settings-fields.ts CONFIG_ONLY_FIELDS.
#   providers: [string]         provider route keys to intercept (default: opencode, opencode-go,
#                               opencode-responses, opencode-anthropic, opencode-google,
#                               opencode-go-responses, opencode-go-anthropic, opencode-go-google — covers every
#                               route this layer declares, including the Google bridge's).
#   userAgent: string           optional custom User-Agent override (default empty = use OpenCode CLI UA).
#   originClient: string        x-opencode-client value (default 'cli').
#   sessionIdEnv: string        env var carrying a caller-supplied session id (default 'OPENCODE_SESSION_ID').
#   freeModelMarker: string     model-id substring getting the core-tool fallback ('*' = all; a blank
#                               value inherits the default 'free'; models the catalog marks free always
#                               qualify).
#   gatewayUrls: [string]       URL substrings marking OpenCode gateway traffic (default both
#                               families: ['opencode.ai/zen', 'opencode.ai/inference']).
#   usageBaseURL: string        OpenCode Go gateway base URL (default 'https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1').
#   credentialOrg: string       org id (wrk_...) sent with an account credential that came from elsewhere.
#   maxContextWindow: number    optional ceiling clamping model context windows (e.g. 131072).
#   modelOverrides: object      per-model overrides for contextWindow, maxTokens and metadata (default {}).
#   modelRoutes: object         per-model wire routing: { <id>: { api, baseURL } } (default {}).
#   debug: true|false           log every streamed call that receives the header to the console.
#   debugFile: path             optional JSONL file for the request and stream debug entries; naming
#                               it writes the file whether or not debug is on.
- insert:
    - id: dsh-opencode-patch
      name: "dsh-opencode-patch"
      config:
        providers:
          - opencode
          - opencode-go
          - opencode-responses
          - opencode-anthropic
          - opencode-google
          - opencode-go-responses
          - opencode-go-anthropic
          - opencode-go-google
        injectUserAgent: true
        userAgent: ""
        injectOriginHeaders: true
        injectCoreTools: true
        enrichModels: true
        usageEnabled: true
        debug: false

dsh-opencode-patch

OpenCode on DeepSeek Harness
Gateway origin headers · Session affinity · Free-tier tool fallback · Live dual-mode quota meter

Quick Start · What this fixes · Interface · Configuration · Troubleshooting · Changelog · Contributing

---

`dsh-opencode-patch` is a DeepSeek Harness host plugin that keeps **OpenCode Zen & Go** models working inside DSH. Connect `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`, `qwen3.8-flash` and the rest of the OpenCode catalog without network rejections, Cloudflare challenges, entitlement mismatches, or invisible limits.
**The default state.** Point DSH at OpenCode with no plugin and the models do not work at all — not on one shape, on any of them:

- **The request is not recognised as coming from a coding agent.** DSH sends its own `User-Agent`, and no `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project` or `x-opencode-session` at all, so the gateway sees an anonymous SDK call and the traffic falls under the abuse rules the vendor documents for clients that do not identify themselves. **The free tier is a separate matter and this is not its cause**: with every one of those headers restored, a CLI `User-Agent`, a valid session id and the `read`/`bash` tool schemas the fallback injects, a Zen `-free` model still answers `403 FreeTierError` from outside OpenCode while a paid model on the same request answers `200`. The ids are still offered — the refusal names itself, and hiding a row the vendor may serve is the worse failure — and the headers it restores are for the paid routes and the vendor's stated client rules.
- **A turn without a session id is rejected or left unlinked.** Every turn has to carry a stable `ses_…`-shaped id, and DSH omits `sessionId` entirely for subagents, background evaluations and modes like **Auto Review**.
- **Free-tier `/responses` bodies are refused without `read` and `bash` in `tools`**, and DSH deliberately d

**What is left once those work is a different problem, and it is not about the account.** OpenCode serves its models on **four different API shapes**, while DSH picks a transport from the provider row — one route can speak one shape. So a model served on Responses, Messages or Mistral answers `500` the moment the basics are restored, which is why this plugin routes per **model** rather than per provider.

**What this does.** It restores every missing protocol element at the network layer — **strictly for OpenCode routes** (`opencode` / `opencode-go` / `opencode-responses` / `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-google`). All other traffic (DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub) passes through untouched.

**What you get.** A picker listing the whole OpenCode catalog with real names, prices and context windows; every model sent to the endpoint it is actually served on; and a live meter for the quota or the spend — no configuration.

**Three things it is built around.**

1. **Minimal intrusion.** Nothing is patched globally: requests are intercepted only for the routes this plugin claims, and every other provider — DeepSeek, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub — passes through byte-identical. The composer meter is one switch away from being gone, not one screen away from being tolerated.
2. **A native DSH plugin.** One `apply()`, a settings card bound to its own namespace, services declared through `ctx.inject`, slots filled the way the host fills its own, and copy in both bundled languages. No private hooks, no patched host code.
3. **OpenCode API compatibility.** The traits the gateways actually check are restored at the network layer — a `ses_…` id shaped exactly like the CLI's own, official origin headers, parent-session lineage, and the free-tier `read`/`bash` schema fallback.

- 🔑 Deterministic `ses_<12hex><14base62>` session hashing with KV-cache affinity across turns, subagents and forks
- 🌐 Gateway origin restoration — `User-Agent`, `x-opencode-client`, `x-opencode-project`, parent-session lineage
- 🧰 Free-tier `read` + `bash` tool-schema fallback, so a free-tier body carries the tool definitions its endpoint requires — one cause of a `403` removed, and not the whole of it: the gateway's gate is not in the request, measured
- 📇 OpenCode-catalog-backed (`models.opencode.ai`, the registry models.dev publishes) with offline shims and background SWR refresh — names, context windows, prices
- ⭕ Live dual-mode composer meter — Go quota ring (5-hour / weekly / monthly) or Zen pay-as-you-go pill, plus session spend and model rate
- 🕵️ Strict credential isolation — Zen keys (`oc_sk_…`) never query the Go quota endpoint

**1. Install** into your DSH Web profile (Node 24+):

```sh
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web
npm install dsh-opencode-patch
```

The package is `dsh-opencode-patch` under every name it is used by: the dependency you install, the bundle entry in your profile, and the row the host resolves. It is also published as [`@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch), and the older name [`@viztor/dsh-opencode`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@viztor/dsh-opencode) keeps publishing as a deprecated thin wrapper that re-exports it — an install still on that name keeps working, and moving to either of the other two is a rename rather than a fix.

**4. Restart `dsh web`.** The host bundle is only imported at boot (`hmr root: []`), so a restart is what loads `lib/index.mjs`; client UI changes (`lib/client.js`) only need a browser refresh.

Done — the **OpenCode Patch** card appears under _Settings → Plugins_, and the meter mounts in the composer dock as soon as an OpenCode model is active.

---

| Without the patch | With `dsh-opencode-patch` |
| :-- | :-- |
| Zen free models fail with `403 FreeTierError` | **Offered, and refused in the gateway's own words.** The headers and tool fallbacks are restored for the paid routes, but they are not this error's cause — measured with all of them in place, a Zen `-free` id still answers `403` while a paid model answers `200`, and the refusal comes from the service behind the console rather than from anything a request carries. So the ids stay in the picker and the refusal surfaces as `400 free_tier_restricted` instead of a hidden row |
| Only one API shape can be served per route — the rest answer `500` once the basics work | **Per-model routing** — each model dispatched to the endpoint its own SDK names, read from the catalog |
| Session IDs rejected with `400 MissingSessionID` | **Deterministic `ses_…` session hashing** and affinity across turns |
| Subagents lose conversation context | **Parent session tracking** (`x-opencode-parent-session-id`, `x-parent-session-id`) |
| Auto Review calls fail with `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | **Fallback session turn capture** preserving turn state across eval calls |
| Quotas and balances are

**Both endpoints, and both credential shapes.** OpenCode's catalog defines an endpoint at two levels: a **provider default** — `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` for Zen, `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` for Go — and a per-model **inference** endpoint that overrides it when the catalog sets one (the CLI reads `model.api.url`, falling back to the provider default). The plugin pins neither: it matches the `opencode.ai/zen` marker, so a model served from the default and a model served from its own endpoint are both patched.

Those endpoints authenticate in **two ways**, because they speak three wire shapes: the OpenAI planes send `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, the Anthropic plane sends `x-api-key: <key>`. The plugin reads **both** — `Authorization` first, then `x-api-key` / `api-key` — so a credential is captured whichever plane carried it, and the Go quota read still finds a key.

The gateway serves four protocol families, and **OpenAI alone is two of them**: Chat Completions and Responses are different wire formats, not two names for one thing. A model that needs Responses does not work on the completions endpoint, and the gateway does not fall back — it answers `500`.

DSH speaks three of the four families itself. The fourth — Google Generative AI — is served by **this patch's own adapter**, registered on the host's `llm` service under the route `opencode-google`, so all four are routed. See the table below.

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text: Zen's provider-level SDK is `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`. models.dev names a **different** SDK per model only when that model needs one, so the presence of `provider.npm` is the signal — and it is what decides the wire protocol. Nothing is matched by hand:

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text:
| models.dev `provider.npm` | models | protocol | served from |
| :-- | --: | :-- | :-- |
| _(absent)_ | 25 | OpenAI Chat Completions | the route you configured |
| `@ai-sdk/openai` | 31 | OpenAI Responses | `opencode-responses` |
| `@ai-sdk/anthropic` | 17 | Anthropic Messages | `opencode-anthropic` |
| `@ai-sdk/google` | 8 | Google Generative AI | `opencode-google` |
| `@ai-sdk/mistral` | 1 | _(a dialect this plugin does not serve)_ | **not offered** |

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text: Counts are the **82** active `opencode` models in `models.opencode.ai` as of 2026-11-04 — everything else the vendor lists is deprecated or retired, and the patch ships only what the gateway still serves. The same 82 are bundled offline in `src/catalog-data.ts`, so every one of them routes correctly before the first catalog refresh; regenerate that file with `pnpm run catalog:shim -- --write` (without `--write` it only checks).

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text: The patch **keeps those two routes out of both the model picker and _Settings → Models_**. Three properties hold today, and one does not yet:

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text:
- **You keep choosing.** The picker shows exactly the models you listed, and each one is matched to the right protocol automatically. OpenCode serves models on three shapes — OpenAI Chat Completions (the default), OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages — and a model that needs one of the other two is dispatched to the route that speaks it. No second route to declare by hand.
- **You are never offered a model that cannot work.** Every one of the four families is reachable, so no model is dropped for want of a protocol: the `@ai-sdk/google` models are served through the patch's own adapter, and the three DSH already speaks are dispatched to the route that speaks them. That holds for models you list by hand as well — one the catalog does not describe is routed by the family its id names (`gemini-*` to the Generative AI path, `claude-*` to Messages), and if the route you put it on cannot serve that protocol it is not offered there at all, rather than answering `400 ModelProtocolUnsupported` when you pick it.
- **One credential, from wherever you already have one.** A routed model authenticates with the key you configured, resolved through the credentials service and never re-asked fo

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text:
**The route, if you would rather declare it yourself:** `opencode-responses` — and `opencode-anthropic`, once you use an Anthropic-plane model — can live in your profile's `llm-pi-ai` `providers` block, listing the models it serves. Declaring it is a choice, not a requirement:

```yaml
opencode-responses:
  api: openai-responses
  baseURL: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1
  headers:

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text: **The plugin registers that route for you**, so the block above is optional. `responses-provider.ts` mounts the host's own `llm-pi-ai` in-process, isolated from the authorization and settings seams and behind an `llm` facade that forwards only the adapter registration — so the route lands without duplicating the catalog directory, the settings namespace, or a single sign-in flow. This is verified against the real harness, not a stub: the route registers, the host's 41 catalog entries and 41 sign-in flows are untouched, and unloading withdraws the route again.

readme.section: 3. How a model's protocol is chosen — and why you configure nothing
readme.text:
The routes inherit **your** credential: each one names the same `apiKeyEnv` your `opencode` route already declares, so a custom key reference is never asked for twice. Routes your profile already declares are left alone — the plugin defers to your model list rather than overriding it.

If your host has no loaded `llm-pi-ai` entry, the plugin registers nothing and says so in the log; declare the route in your profile in that case.

| Mode | What the patch does |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Interactive multi-turn chat** | KV prompt-cache affinity via a stable per-session `ses_…` id |
| **Subagents & forks** | Child and parent sessions both hashed; lineage carried in parent headers |
| **Agent teams** | Shared-workspace attribution preserved across orchestration turns |
| **Experimental Auto Review** | Background audit calls with an omitted `sessionId` still get a deterministic turn state, headers and tool fallback — and they take their route from the session, so the model the session is on is the model they run |

readme.section: 5. The catalog: what gets merged, and what wins
readme.text:
The model list is assembled from four sources, each answering a different question:

| Source | Answers |
| :-- | :-- |
| Bundled shim | what can be offered before any network call — cold start, offline |
| `models.opencode.ai` | the canonical spec, price and display name |
| The gateway's `/models` | what **this account** actually has |
| Discovery decoration | what `discoverModels` should answer |

readme.section: 5. The catalog: what gets merged, and what wins
readme.text: Merging is **additive**: adapter rows are kept, canonical rows are appended when a model is missing, and a row is dropped only when the registry marks it `status: "deprecated"` — a fact, not a guess. Display names and prices come from the catalog (`models.opencode.ai`), because a gateway listing carries ids and little else.

readme.section: 5. The catalog: what gets merged, and what wins
readme.text: Two things follow that you will notice in use. **Cold start is never empty** — the bundled shim answers before the first refresh, so the picker has models immediately. And **a model the catalog has no row for still appears**, with `—` where its rate would be: never a guess, and never the previous model's name.

readme.section: 5. The catalog: what gets merged, and what wins
readme.text: Both generated files are checked in CI (`catalog:shim`, `limits:shim`); they exit non-zero when the vendor's data moved, which is the only way to notice the vendor's registry changing under you. A pull request fails on that only when it changes the code that generates the file; otherwise CI warns, and a nightly run proposes the refresh as a pull request of its own.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: Two questions decide where a request goes, and the **Account & Endpoint** section is where you answer them.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: **Which endpoint family.** The gateway answers on two families — the older `/zen/v1` (`/zen/go/v1` on Go), one base for every protocol, and the newer per-protocol `inference` family (`/inference/openai/v1`, `/inference/anthropic/v1`, `/inference/google/v1beta`, with `/inference/go/…` on Go) — and they are entitled **separately**: an account that works on one is not guaranteed to work on the other. `modern` sends each protocol to its own inference path; `auto`, the default, is an alias of `modern`; `legacy` pins the older family, which is what you want when your account only works there.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: **Which credential wins.** `keySource` orders the sources the plugin can see — `auto` prefers a key you declared, then one captured from a live request, then the declared reference; `request` promotes a captured key first; `configured` does the reverse. Below it, `readOpencodeStore` lets the plugin read the credential OpenCode itself stored, as the **last** resort only. Both are `off`/`auto` by default, so nothing changes until you say so.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text:
Override-style knobs (literal strings, markers, route lists) are deliberately **config-only** so a default fits every documented setup — see [Configuration Reference](#-configuration-reference).

The composer panel also shows the **session's accumulated cost and the active model's per-million-token rate**, and there is no switch for it: it is part of the panel rather than an option, so it is on whenever the panel is.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text:
The card also carries a **live Go usage summary** above the controls — the same reading the composer meter shows, in the layout the vendor's own console uses: one row per window, with what is **left** held out on the right.

```
Go usage                                           Healthy
● 5 hours    0% used · resets in 4h 58m           100% left
● Weekly    28% used · resets in 3d 2h             72% left
● Monthly   14% used · resets Nov 7, 8:55 AM       86% left

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: **This build carries the API key path only.** There is no sign-in row and no device flow: a credential comes from the deployment's configuration, from a key captured on a live request, or — when `readOpencodeStore` is on — from the OpenCode installation's own store. The Console login (device flow, session store, credential pool) lives on the `v2` line and is deliberately not in `main`, so nothing here depends on a service the host may not mount.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: **If the card looks like the previous build after updating, the host process has not restarted.** The host bundle is read once at process start, so a browser reload keeps running the previous `lib/index.mjs`; stop and restart `dsh web`. The row is the quickest way to tell, because it is new in the same build as everything else.

readme.section: Choosing the endpoint and the credential
readme.text: "Left" is a percentage, never a dollar figure: `/usage` publishes a percent per window and no balance at all, and the plan tier is not discoverable — so a dollar remainder would be a guess. The ⓘ states that. A quota that cannot be read says so and prints no numbers, rather than a row of zeroes that reads as a measurement.

The meter mounts next to DSH's native `ContextMeter` in `conversation.composer.dock`:

Per-state behaviour — the trigger's three states, both panels, what every row answers, and the three different kinds of "no number" — is documented in [docs/quota-meter.md](./docs/quota-meter.md).

- **Adaptive ring**: a real-time SVG ring for the window that answers the question. A window that is **out** — rate-limited, or at its cap — is shown, widest first (monthly → weekly → 5-hour), because a monthly cap explains a refusal the 5-hour window does not. Otherwise it shows the **5-hour** window, which resets soonest and so is the one you can still act on. On a **free model** the ring renders hollow in the muted track colour — the plan's limit says nothing about a bill that cannot be charged, and red against `$0.00` would read as "you are out of money".
- **Semantic colors**: green below 80% (`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary`), amber at ≥80% (`--dsw-alias-state-warn-primary`), red at the cap (`--dsw-alias-state-error-primary`).
- **Click panel**: three window rows with live reset countdowns and a bar per window, a session-spend row naming the **currently selected** model, a Zen-overflow row, a rate-limited alert, and act-on-it links. Hovering the trigger shows a `Tooltip` listing **every** window (`5 hours 11% · Weekly 33% · Monthly 16%`), because the trigger can print only one of them and the next question is always "and the other two?".
- **A model the catalog has no pric

A Zen route renders no Go figure anywhere: there is no ring at all (a gauge with no measurement is decoration), the label is the spend rather than a percentage, a rate-limited **Go** plan does not paint the **Zen** trigger as an alert, and hovering carries the price (`Session Spend $0.00 · Pay-as-you-go`). A Go window is a fact about a plan this route never bills against, so it does not appear here.

- **Zen trigger**: the spend as its label, and **no ring** — the ring is a gauge, and Zen has no window to measure (`$0.00` before anything has been priced, `$0.42` after). The figure is the only real number available — OpenCode exposes Zen balance through console server actions that require a browser session, so an API key cannot read it.
- **Pay-as-you-go panel**: header with a `Pay-as-you-go` badge, the session-spend row (when the price switch is on), and one link — [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console), labelled **Top up**, because top-up is what a pay-as-you-go user wants from that page and it has no URL of its own.

**The monthly allowance, and why it is a total and not a balance.** The three windows are shares of a per-model monthly **dollar** allowance — the vendor's own words: _"Usage limits are defined as monthly dollar amounts… 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%."_ So the meter prints that allowance under the windows: for `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `Go $60 · Plus $120`. It is generated from the vendor's Go documentation (`pnpm run limits:shim`, checked on a schedule in CI) because the page states outright that _"usage limits may change"_ — a hand-typed table would be wrong within a release, and a stale dollar figure looks authoritative.

It shows **both tiers** rather than one, because the plan is not discoverable: `/limits`, `/plan`, `/subscription`, `/account` and `/credits` all return 404, and `/models` carries no limit. Guessing a tier would misstate the money by 2–3x.

It is deliberately **not** a remaining balance. `GET /zen/go/v1/usage` takes no model parameter, so its percentages describe the account rather than the model you are reading — multiplying an account-level percentage by a per-model allowance yields a number with no referent. The remaining balance is in the console, where it is exact.

**Zen balance & overflow.** If an `OPENCODE_API_KEY` (or `oc_sk_...`) is configured, Zen pay-as-you-go is detected automatically. The Zen panel carries **no balance row**: OpenCode exposes that balance only through console server actions that need a browser session, so the panel links straight to the [OpenCode Console](https://opencode.ai/console) rather than freeze a number it cannot keep current. The balance row lives on the **Go** panel instead, where it answers a question the panel can answer — whether an over-limit Go request will really be billed to that balance.

**Verified on DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1` — both the `alpha` and `rc` channels (Node 24+)**

The harness publishes two **channels**, `alpha` and `rc`, and they are parallel tracks rather than a version ordering: semver sorts `0.2.1-rc.2` _above_ `0.2.1-alpha.5`. The plugin targets two lines on both channels: **`0.2.1`**, whose `rc` builds `dsh@latest` still carries, and the **`0.2.2`** prereleases on both channels: `alpha` is at `0.2.2-alpha.3`, and `rc` opened the line with `0.2.2-rc.1` (published under the `next` dist-tag; the test install runs `0.2.2-alpha.2`). The `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` peer range says so exactly:

The first clause covers the `0.2.1` line on both channels: its lower bound (`alpha.1`) sorts below every `rc` of the same line, so rc needs no separate entry. The second is **not** redundant — semver excludes prereleases unless a comparator in the same `major.minor.patch` tuple carries one, so `<0.3.0` alone would silently drop every `0.2.2-*` build, alpha and rc alike. Both clauses stop at `0.3.0`, which leaves the next line a separate decision rather than a silent widening.

The optional `@deepseek-ai/cordis` peer follows the typert range. Each line moved the host core: the `0.2.1` builds peer `~4.0.5` (or a `4.0.5` prerelease), the `0.2.2` alphas a `4.0.6` prerelease, and `0.2.2-rc.1` `~4.1.0`. A fresh install takes the cordis the **newest** admitted typert build peers on, so a cordis peer that misses it fails with `ERESOLVE`; one that misses an older line's cordis fails beside a host already installed on that line. ---

`dsh-opencode-patch` 是一个 DeepSeek Harness 宿主插件，让 **OpenCode Zen 与 Go** 模型在 DSH 内持续可用。无需遭遇网络拒绝、Cloudflare 挑战、权益不匹配或隐形限制，即可接入 `claude-sonnet-4-5`、`gpt-5.4`、`gemini-3.8-flash`、`deepseek-v4.1-flash`、`muse-spark-1.3-contributor-free`、`qwen3.8-flash` 以及 OpenCode 目录中的其余模型。

**默认状态。** 把 DSH 直接指向 OpenCode、不装任何插件，模型是**完全不能用**的——不是某一种形状不能用，而是全部：

- **请求不会被识别为"编码 agent"发出的。** DSH 发的是自己的 `User-Agent`，不带 `x-opencode-client`、`x-opencode-project`，也不带 `x-opencode-session`；网关看到的就是一次匿名 SDK 调用，流量要受厂商对"不表明身份的客户端"所设的滥用规则约束。**免费层是另一回事，原因也不在这里**：把这些请求头全部恢复、换上 CLI 的 `User-Agent`、带上有效的会话 id 以及回退注入的 `read`/`bash` 工具定义之后，在 OpenCode 之外调用 Zen 的 `-free` 模型仍然返回 `403 FreeTierError`，而同一个请求换成付费模型返回 `200`。这些 id 依然会列出——拒绝本身会说明原因，而把厂商可能仍在服务的模型藏起来是更糟的失败——补丁恢复的请求头服务于付费路由以及厂商声明的客户端规则。
- **没有会话 id 的一轮会被拒、或失去关联。** 每一轮都必须带一个稳定的 `ses_…` 形状的 id，而 DSH 在子代理、后台评估以及 **Auto Review** 这类模式下会完全省略 `sessionId`。
- **免费层的 `/responses` 请求体缺少 `read` 与 `bash` 会被拒**，而 DSH 是刻意不发这两个工具的。
- **目录很单薄。** 裸 `/models` 列表只有 id，几乎没有别的信息，所以选择器里是一堆没有名字、没有价格、没有上下文窗口的行。

**这些能用之后剩下的**是另一个问题，而且与账号无关：OpenCode 的模型分布在**四种不同的 API 形状**上，而 DSH 是按 provider 行选择传输协议的——一条路由只能说一种形状。所以走 Responses / Messages / Mistral 的模型在基础问题解决之后就会返回 `500`。这正是插件**按模型而不是按 provider** 路由的原因。

插件在网络层补齐所有缺失的协议要素——**且仅针对 OpenCode 路由**（`opencode` / `opencode-go` / `opencode-responses` / `opencode-anthropic` / `opencode-google`）。其余全部流量（DeepSeek、OpenAI、Anthropic、GitHub）原样通过。

**三条主线。**

1. **最小侵入。** 不做全局补丁：只拦截本插件声明的路由，其他厂商——DeepSeek、OpenAI、Anthropic、GitHub——的请求原样通过。计量器离"彻底消失"只差一个开关，而不是离"勉强忍受"隔着一个页面。
2. **原生 DSH 插件。** 一个 `apply()`、一张绑定自己命名空间的设置卡、用 `ctx.inject` 声明服务、按宿主自己的方式填充插槽，文案随宿主语言切换。没有私有钩子，不改宿主代码。
3. **OpenCode API 兼容。** 网关真正检查的那些特征在网络层还原——与 CLI 同形状的 `ses_…` 会话 id、官方来源头、父会话血统，以及免费层的 `read`/`bash` 工具 schema 回退。

**亮点**

- 🔑 确定性的 `ses_<12hex><14base62>` 会话哈希，跨轮次、子代理与分叉保持 KV 缓存亲和
- 🌐 网关来源恢复——`User-Agent`、`x-opencode-client`、`x-opencode-project`、父会话谱系
- 🧰 免费层 `read` + `bash` 工具 schema 回退，让免费层的请求体带上它的端点所要求的工具定义——这去掉的是 `403` 的一个成因，而不是全部：网关的那道闸不在请求里，实测如此
- 📇 基于 OpenCode 官方目录（`models.opencode.ai`，即 models.dev 发布的那份注册表）的模型目录，带离线预置与后台 SWR 刷新——名称、上下文窗口、价格
- ⭕ 实时双模式停靠栏计量——Go 额度环（5 小时 / 每周 / 每月）或 Zen 按量计费胶囊，外加会话消耗与模型费率
- 🕵️ 严格凭据隔离——Zen 密钥（`oc_sk_…`）绝不查询 Go 额度端点

**2. 启用 bundle**——把该包加入 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` 数组：

| :-- | :-- |
| Zen 免费模型报 `403 FreeTierError` | **照常列出，由网关用自己的话拒绝。** 请求头与工具回退会为付费路由恢复，但它们不是这个错误的原因——在全部就位的情况下实测，Zen 的 `-free` id 仍返回 `403`，而付费模型返回 `200`；拒绝来自控制台背后的服务，而不是请求携带的任何内容。所以这些 id 留在选择器里，拒绝以 `400 free_tier_restricted` 呈现，而不是变成一行被隐藏的模型 |
| 一条路由只能说一种形状——基础问题解决后，其余模型返回 `500` | **逐模型路由**——按目录里每个模型自己声明的 SDK 派发到对应端点 |
| 会话 ID 被拒并返回 `400 MissingSessionID` | **确定性的 `ses_…` 会话哈希**与跨轮次亲和 |
| 子代理丢失对话上下文 | **父会话跟踪**（`x-opencode-parent-session-id`、`x-parent-session-id`） |
| Auto Review 调用报 `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | **回退会话轮次捕获**，在评估调用之间保留轮次状态 |
| 额度与余额不可见 | **实时双模式停靠栏计量**，显示 Go 额度或 Zen 按量计费 |
| Zen 密钥在 Go 用量上触发 `403 EntitlementError` | **严格凭据隔离**，让 Zen 密钥不接触 Go 端点 |

readme.section: 🧭 支持的模型与多协议路由
readme.text:
**两种端点，两种凭据形状。** OpenCode 的目录在两个层级上定义端点：**provider 默认端点**——Zen 是 `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`，Go 是 `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1`——以及**逐模型的推理端点**，目录里设置时会覆盖默认值（CLI 读 `model.api.url`，取不到就回落到 provider 默认）。插件**两个都不钉死**：它匹配的是 `opencode.ai/zen` 这个标记，所以走默认端点的模型和走自己端点的模型都会被补丁覆盖。

这些端点的认证有**两种**，因为它们说三种线格式：OpenAI 那两个平面发 `Authorization: Bearer <key>`，Anthropic 平面发 `x-api-key: <key>`。插件**两种都读**——先 `Authorization`，再 `x-api-key` / `api-key`——所以凭据无论由哪个平面带过来都能被捕获，Go 额度查询也仍然找得到密钥。

readme.section: 🧭 支持的模型与多协议路由
readme.text:
网关提供四种线路家族，而 **OpenAI 自己就占了两种**：Chat Completions 与 Responses 是**两种不同的线路格式**，不是同一个东西的两个名字。需要 Responses 的模型在 completions 端点上不工作，而网关**不会回退**——它直接返回 `500`。

DSH 能说其中四种，插件就把这四种都路由掉。**Google Generative AI 走插件自己挂的路由 `opencode-google`** ——它曾经是唯一没有路由的一种，现在不是了。见下表。

readme.section: 1. OpenCode Zen (`provider: opencode`) — 按量计费与免费额度

readme.section: 3. 模型的协议是怎么定的 —— 以及为什么你什么都不用配
readme.text:
数量为 `models.opencode.ai` 中 `opencode` 的 82 个**在用**模型，统计于 2026-11-04 —— 其余已废弃或下架，补丁只内置网关仍在服务的部分。同样这 82 个模型离线内置在 `src/catalog-data.ts`，因此在第一次 catalog 刷新之前它们每一个路由都是正确的；用 `pnpm run catalog:shim -- --write` 重新生成该文件（不加 `--write` 时只做检查）。

插件把这两条内部路由同时挡在模型选择器和 _Settings → Models_ 之外。**三条性质今天就成立，还有一条尚未成立：**

readme.section: 3. 模型的协议是怎么定的 —— 以及为什么你什么都不用配
readme.text:
- **你的挑选仍然有效。** 选择器显示的就是你列出的模型，每个模型都会**自动匹配到正确的协议**。OpenCode 的模型分布在三种形状上——OpenAI Chat Completions（默认）、OpenAI Responses、Anthropic Messages——需要后两种的模型会被派发到对应路由。不需要手工声明第二条路由。
- **永远不会提供跑不通的模型。** 那 8 个 `@ai-sdk/google` 模型由插件自己的适配器服务（路由 `opencode-google`），所以它们**不再被剔除**——插件曾经没有对应协议，现在有了。真正会被剔除的是 `@ai-sdk/mistral` 的那一个：它的方言网关怎么回答还没有测过，所以宁可不提供，也不送它去一个凭空想出来的地方。
- **一份凭据。** 所有路由模型共用你已配置的 `opencode` key，经凭据服务解析，**不会重新问你要**。

readme.section: 3. 模型的协议是怎么定的 —— 以及为什么你什么都不用配
readme.text:
**如果你更想自己声明路由**：`opencode-responses`（以及你用上 Anthropic 平面模型后的 `opencode-anthropic`）可以写进 profile 的 `llm-pi-ai` `providers` 块里，并列出它服务的模型。声明是一个选择，不是要求：

```yaml
opencode-responses:
  api: openai-responses
  baseURL: https://opencode.ai/zen/v1
  headers:

readme.section: 3. 模型的协议是怎么定的 —— 以及为什么你什么都不用配
readme.text:
**这条路由由插件替你注册**，所以上面那段配置是可选的。`responses-provider.ts` 会在进程内挂载宿主自己的 `llm-pi-ai`：隔离 authorization 与 settings 两个接缝，并在一层只转发 adapter 注册的 `llm` 门面之后挂载——因此它既不会重复登记整个 catalog 目录、settings 命名空间，也不会多注册任何一条 sign-in flow。这一版是对着真实 harness 验证的，不是桩：路由注册成功，宿主自己的 41 条 catalog 与 41 条 sign-in flow 原封不动，卸载时该路由被撤回。

这些路由继承**你的**凭据：每一条都沿用你 `opencode` 路由已经声明的同一个 `apiKeyEnv`，所以自定义的 key 引用不需要你再说一遍。你在 profile 里已经声明过的路由会被尊重——插件不会覆盖你的模型列表。

若宿主没有已加载的 `llm-pi-ai` 条目，插件不会注册任何东西，只会在日志里说明；此时请在 profile 里显式声明该路由。

| 模式 | 补丁做什么 |
| :-- | :-- |
| **交互式多轮对话** | 通过每会话稳定的 `ses_…` id 提供 KV 提示缓存亲和 |
| **子代理与分叉** | 子、父会话都参与哈希；谱系由父级请求头携带 |
| **Agent 团队** | 跨编排轮次保留共享工作区的归属信息 |
| **实验性 Auto Review** | 即使后台审计调用省略 `sessionId`，仍会得到确定性的轮次状态、请求头与工具回退——而且它们的路由取自会话，所以会话正在用哪个模型，它们就跑哪个模型 |

---

readme.section: 5. 目录：合并了什么，谁说了算
readme.text:
模型清单由四个来源拼成，每个来源回答的是不同的问题：

| 来源                 | 回答                                           |
| :------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- |
| 内置 shim            | 一次网络请求都还没有时能提供什么——冷启动、离线 |
| `models.opencode.ai` | 规范参数、价格与显示名                         |
| 网关的 `/models`     | **这个账号**实际能用什么                       |
| 发现装饰             | `discoverModels` 该回答什么                    |

readme.section: 5. 目录：合并了什么，谁说了算
readme.text:
合并是**增量式**的：适配器给的行保留，规范行只在缺失时追加，只有当目录（registry）把某个模型标为 `status: "deprecated"` 时才省略它——那是事实，不是猜测。显示名与价格取自目录（`models.opencode.ai`），因为网关列表只给 id，别的几乎没有。

有两点你在使用中会注意到。**冷启动永远不为空**——内置 shim 在第一次刷新前就能回答，选择器立刻有模型可选。而且**目录里没有条目的模型照样出现**，费率位置显示 `—`：既不猜，也不会退回去显示上一个模型的名字。

两个生成文件都在 CI 里校验（`catalog:shim`、`limits:shim`）；厂商数据变动时它们以非零码退出——这是唯一能发现厂商注册表在你背后变了的办法。只有当拉取请求改动了生成该文件的代码时，CI 才会因此失败；否则只给出警告，由每晚的任务以单独的拉取请求提出刷新。

| 界面 | 位置 | 显示什么 |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **计量表触发按钮** | 输入框停靠栏，模型选择器旁 | Go：圆环 + 该窗口的百分比。Zen：本会话消费额，**不画圆环** |
| **计量表面板** | 点击触发按钮 | 三个窗口、月度额度、本会话消耗、Zen 余额、操作链接 |
| **设置卡片** | _Settings → Plugins → OpenCode 补丁设置_ | 九个控件，上方另有一份实时 Go 用量摘要 |

悬停触发按钮解释它自己的数字；点击打开面板。下面逐节展示每个界面，逐状态的行为见 [docs/quota-meter.zh-CN.md](./docs/quota-meter.zh-CN.md)。

readme.section: 设置卡片 — _Settings → Plugins → OpenCode 补丁设置_
readme.text: 四个分区共九个控件——都是用户真正会做出的决定。所有控件都基于平台自身的原语渲染（`Switch`、`Tag`、`Button`、宿主 token），每个配置项都带提示以及恢复默认的操作。

readme.section: 设置卡片 — _Settings → Plugins → OpenCode 补丁设置_
readme.text:
| 分区 | 控件 | 默认 | 作用 |
| :-- | :-- | :-: | :-- |
| **网关请求** | 恢复 User-Agent（默认开启） | `on` | 恢复官方 OpenCode CLI 的 `User-Agent`，使 Cloudflare WAF 校验通过 |
| **网关请求** | 注入客户端来源头（默认开启） | `on` | 在网关流量上注入 `x-opencode-client`（以及来源请求头集合） |
| **网关请求** | 附带工作区项目标识（默认开启） | `on` | 用当前文件夹名标记 `x-opencode-project`；关闭则省略该请求头 |
| **模型与免费额度** | 用 OpenCode 官方目录补全模型信息（默认开启） | `on` | 把目录的上下文上限、模态与思考档位补进模型信息，并让网关 `/models` 列表带上完整目录。**不会**往选择器里添加模型——选择器只显示已声明的；要添加请用卡片的**检查目录** |
| **模型与免费额度** | 自动补全核心工具（默认开启） | `on` | 补上免费层 `/responses` 请求体所需的 `read` + `bash` schema |
| **配额计量** | 开启输入区用量计量（默认开启） | `on` | 在输入框停靠栏挂载实时计量表——Go 额度环，或 Zen 会话消耗 |
| **账户与端点** | API 端点 | `auto` | 请求发往哪个端点家族：**自动**（同新端点） · **旧端点**（`zen/v1`、`zen/go/v1`） · **新端点**（按协议的 `inference/{openai,anthropic,google}/…`，Go 为 `inference/go/…`） |
| **账户与端点** | 凭据来源 | `auto` | 多个密钥同时可用时以哪个为准：**自动** · **优先实时请求** · **优先已声明密钥** |
| **账户与端点** | 读取 OpenCode 安装版的密钥（默认关闭） | `off` | 允许本插件读取 OpenCode 自己保存的凭据，且仅作最后手段——默认关闭 |

一个请求发往哪里由两个问题决定，答案就在**账户与端点**分区里。

**发往哪个端点家族。** 网关在两套端点上都应答——较早的 `/zen/v1`（Go 为 `/zen/go/v1`），所有协议共用一个基址；以及较新的按协议划分的 `inference` 家族（`/inference/openai/v1`、`/inference/anthropic/v1`、`/inference/google/v1beta`，Go 为 `/inference/go/…`）——而两者的授权是**彼此独立**的：在一边可用的账户不保证在另一边可用。`modern` 将每个协议发往各自的 inference 路径；`auto`（默认值）是 `modern` 的别名；`legacy` 固定使用较早的一套，适用于账户只在那里可用的情况。

**以哪个凭据为准。** `keySource` 决定插件可见的多个凭据源的优先级——`auto` 优先使用你声明过的密钥，其次是从实时请求中捕获的密钥，最后是声明的凭据引用；`request` 把捕获到的密钥提到最前；`configured` 则相反。其下的 `readOpencodeStore` 允许插件读取 OpenCode 自己保存的凭据，且**仅作最后手段**。两者默认分别为 `auto` 与关闭，因此在你说要改之前一切照旧。

覆盖类配置项（字面字符串、标记、路由列表）刻意只留在配置里，让默认值适用于所有有文档记载的配置——参见[配置参考](#-配置参考)。

卡片在控件上方还带一份**实时的 Go 用量摘要**——和输入框计量表同一个读数，但用官方控制台的排版：每个窗口一行，**剩余**单独放在右侧。

```
Go 用量                                             状态正常
● 5 小时   0% 已用 · 4小时58分钟后重置              100% 剩余
● 每周    28% 已用 · 3天2小时后重置                  72% 剩余
● 每月    14% 已用 · 11月7日8点55分重置              86% 剩余

**这个版本只带 API 密钥路径。** 没有登录行，也没有设备流：凭据来自部署的配置、来自从实际请求中捕获的密钥，或者——在开启 `readOpencodeStore` 时——来自 OpenCode 安装自身的存储。Console 登录（设备流、会话存储、凭据池）在 `v2` 线上，刻意不放进 `main`，因此这里不依赖宿主可能没有挂载的服务。

**如果更新后卡片看起来还是上一版，说明宿主进程没有重启。** 宿主包只在进程启动时读取一次，所以浏览器刷新仍在运行上一版的 `lib/index.mjs`；请停止并重启 `dsh web`。这一行是最快的判断办法，因为它和其他所有改动在同一个版本里新加入。

「剩余」是百分比，不是美元数：`/usage` 每个窗口只给一个百分比、完全没有余额接口，而套餐档位也无法探测——任何美元余额都会是猜的。这一点由 ⓘ 说明。读不到配额时它明说读不到，并且不打印任何数字，而不是打一排会被当成真实读数的 `0%`。

计量表挂载在 `conversation.composer.dock` 中 DSH 原生 `ContextMeter` 旁。逐状态的行为说明（触发按钮的三种状态、两个面板、每一行的含义、三种「没有数字」的区别）见 [`docs/quota-meter.zh-CN.md`](./docs/quota-meter.zh-CN.md)。

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Type a message...                                               │
│                                                                 │
│ [+] Attach                            [DeepSeek V4.1 Flash ⌄] [⬆]│

- **自适应环**：实时 SVG 环，显示能回答问题的那个窗口。**已经用尽**的窗口——受限或到达上限——优先显示，从宽到窄（每月 → 每周 → 5 小时），因为月上限能解释一次拒绝，而 5 小时窗口解释不了。否则显示 **5 小时**窗口：它最早重置，是还能行动的那个。**免费模型**上环形以灰色空心显示——套餐上限与一笔无法产生的账单无关，对着 `$0.00` 亮红色会被读成"你的钱用完了"。
- **语义色**：低于 80% 为绿色（`--dsw-alias-state-success-primary`），≥80% 为琥珀色（`--dsw-alias-state-warn-primary`），达到上限为红色（`--dsw-alias-state-error-primary`）。
- **点击面板**：三行窗口，各带实时重置倒计时与一条进度条；一行会话消耗，写的是**当前选中的**模型；一行 Zen 余额；一条受限告警；以及可直接处理的链接。悬停触发器显示 `Tooltip`，**列出全部三个窗口**（`5 小时 11% · 每周 33% · 每月 16%`）——触发器只能印一个数字，而下一个问题永远是"另外两个呢？"。
- **目录里没有价格的模型显示 `—`，不是 `Free`。** 面板始终显示选择器上的模型名，即使目录里还没有它的条目（目录按计划同步）——显示上一个模型的名字比显示没有价格更糟。

**月度额度，以及为什么它是总额而不是余额。** 三个窗口是某个模型月度**美元**额度的比例——官方原话：_"Usage limits are defined as monthly dollar amounts… 5-hour — 20% of the monthly limit; weekly — 50%; and monthly — 100%."_ 所以计量表把这笔额度打印在窗口下面：`mimo-v2.6-flash` 是 `Go $60 · Plus $120`。它由官方 Go 文档生成（`pnpm run limits:shim`，CI 定时校验），因为页面明说*"usage limits may change"*——手写表一个版本内就会过期，而过期的美元数字看起来很权威。

它同时显示**两个档位**而不是只显示一个，因为档位查不到：`/limits`、`/plan`、`/subscription`、`/account`、`/credits` 全部 404，`/models` 也没有额度字段。猜一个档位，金额就会差 2–3 倍。
它**刻意不是剩余额度**。`GET /zen/go/v1/usage` 不接受 model 参数，所以返回的百分比是账号级的，而额度是按模型的——两者相乘得到的数字没有指代对象。真实余额在控制台，那里是准确的。

Zen 路线上不出现任何 Go 的数字：根本不画圆环（没有可量的量规就是装饰），标签是消费额而不是百分比，Go 套餐被限流也不会把 Zen 按钮染成告警色，悬停则带上价格（`当前会话消耗 $0.00 · 按量计费`）。Go 的窗口是关于一条本路线永不结算的套餐的事实，所以在这里不出现。

- **Zen 触发器**：标签是本会话累计花费（未计价时为 `$0.00`，计价后如 `$0.42`），且**不画圆环**——圆环是量规，而 Zen 没有可量的窗口。这个数字是唯一能拿到的真实数字：OpenCode 的 Zen 余额只能通过 console 的 server action 读取，API 密钥读不到。
- **按量计费面板**：带 `Pay-as-you-go` 徽标的头部、会话消耗行（价格开关开启时），以及一个链接——[OpenCode 控制台](https://opencode.ai/console)，标为**充值**：按量计费的人点进去就是要充钱，而充值本身没有独立的地址。

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  OpenCode Zen                [Pay-as-you-go]  │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Session Spend                                │

**Zen 余额与溢出。** 若配置了 `OPENCODE_API_KEY`（或 `oc_sk_…`），Zen 按量计费会被自动检测。Zen 面板**不显示余额行**：该余额只能通过 console 的 server action 读取，需要浏览器会话，因此面板直接链接到 [OpenCode 控制台](https://opencode.ai/console)，而不是冻结一个无法保持最新的数字。余额行放在 **Go** 面板上——那里它回答的是一个面板真能回答的问题：超出配额的 Go 请求是否真的会从该余额扣费。

---
这些项存在于 schema 中，却不渲染任何控件——每一项都是字面值、标记或引用，其默认值适用于所有有文档记载的配置。它们仍可在该行的 `config` 中编辑；[`cordis.patch.yml`](./cordis.patch.yml) 是参考。

| 配置项 | 默认值 | 保留在配置中的原因 |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| `providers` | `opencode`, `opencode-go`, `opencode-responses`, `opencode-anthropic` | 要拦截的路由 id；必须覆盖本层声明的每一条路由 |
| `gatewayUrls` | `opencode.ai/zen` | 标记网关流量的 URL 子串；只有镜像或中继才会改它们 |
| `userAgent` | 空（= 规范 CLI UA） | 字面覆盖；默认值就是网关所期望的值 |
| `originClient` | `cli` | `x-opencode-client` 的字面值 |
| `sessionIdEnv` | `OPENCODE_SESSION_ID` | 指定一个仅当调用方提供会话 id 时才使用的环境变量名 |
| `freeModelMarker` | `free` | 模型 id 子串；`*` 强制启用回退；留空则沿用默认值；目录标记为免费的模型始终适用 |
| `usageBaseURL` | `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1` | 端点覆盖；从组合中自动发现 |
| `credentialOrg` | — | 账户凭据所属的组织 id，在部署从带外提供一个时使用 |
| `debug` / `debugFile` | `false` / — | 诊断用 JSONL 日志，不是谁会在 UI 里调节的行为 |

> **宿主重载规则：** 任何宿主变更（`lib/index.mjs`）之后都要重启 `dsh web`；客户端 UI 变更（`lib/client.js`）刷新浏览器即可。

---

| 症状 | 可能原因 | 解决方法 |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| 免费模型报 `403 FreeTierError` | 网关的门槛不在请求里：用真实账号、它的会话令牌、它的当前组织以及官方客户端发送的全部请求头实测，免费层模型仍返回 `403` | 上面三个注入开关（**恢复 User-Agent**、**注入客户端来源头**、**自动补全核心工具**）仍值得保持开启——它们让流量可被识别，并恢复工具定义——但单靠它们打不开免费层。付费模型配上密钥即可使用；排除了什么、如何排除，见 [docs/opencode-1.19-api.md](./docs/opencode-1.19-api.md) |
| `400 MissingSessionID` | 未附带会话请求头 | 确认 `dsh-opencode-patch` 已列入 profile 的 `dsh.profile.bundles` |
| Auto Review 报 `TRANSPORT: Connection error` | 更新后宿主进程未重启 | 停止并重启 `dsh web`，让新的 `lib/index.mjs` 加载 |
| Go 模型始终不显示额度环 | 解析不到 Go 凭据，或当前激活的网关不是 `opencode-go` | 在 DSH Credentials 中存储 `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`，并经 `opencode-go` 路由 |
| 目录中的模型在 Settings → Fetch 里缺失，或已下线的模型仍然存在 | 宿主模块过期、补全关闭，或适配器用自带目录作答 | `pnpm run build`、重启 `dsh web`、保持**用 OpenCode 官方目录补全模型信息**开启、从匹配的路由获取、搜索精确 id（如 `space-bunny-free`） |
| 弹出面板以红色显示“已达限额” | 滚动 / 每月窗口已用到 100% | 打开 [OpenCode 控制台](https://opencode.ai/console)并启用 _使用余额（Use balance）_，以溢出到 Zen 额度 |
| 非 OpenCode 模型行为异常 | 与本补丁无关 | 发往其他网关的流量原样通过 |

- **更小的公开 API。** 包入口只导出 `apply`、`Config`、`inject` 和 `name`（宿主读取的名称），以及配置类型（`PluginConfig`、`ResolvedPluginConfig`、`ModelOverrideConfig`、`ModelRouteConfig`、`EndpointFamily`、`KeySourcePolicy`）。此前额外重新导出的其余内容现在都是内部实现。
- **`./src/*` 不再是导出路径。** `src/` 从未包含在发布文件中，所以这个子路径只在仓库内可解析，安装后并不存在。
- **`internalRoutes` 已移除。** 按协议划分的内部路由总是会挂载。仍带有 `internalRoutes` 的 profile 配置行可以通过校验，该键会被忽略。
- **`@viztor/dsh-opencode` 已弃用，但仍在发布。** 它是一个转导出 `dsh-opencode-patch` 的薄包装，所以用旧名的安装照常解析；registry 上标记为弃用并指向正式名称。新安装请用 `dsh-opencode-patch` 或 `@viztor/dsh-opencode-patch`。

**已在 DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1` 上验证 —— `alpha` 与 `rc` 两个通道（Node 24+）**

Harness 按 `alpha` 与 `rc` 两个**通道**发布，它们是平行的发布线而非版本先后：semver 中 `0.2.1-rc.2` 排序在 `0.2.1-alpha.5` **之上**。本插件在两个通道上都针对两条线：**`0.2.1`**（`dsh@latest` 仍停留在它的 `rc` 构建上），以及两个通道上的 **`0.2.2`** 预发布版本：`alpha` 已到 `0.2.2-alpha.3`，`rc` 以 `0.2.2-rc.1` 开启了这条线（发布在 `next` dist-tag 下；测试安装运行的是 `0.2.2-alpha.2`）。`@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol` 的 peer 范围正是这么写的：

```
>=0.2.1-alpha.1 <0.3.0 || >=0.2.2-0 <0.3.0
```

第一个子句覆盖两个通道上的 `0.2.1` 整条线：下界 `alpha.1` 排序低于同线的所有 `rc`，因此无需单独枚举 rc。第二个子句**并不多余**——除非同一 `major.minor.patch` 的某个比较符带有预发布号，semver 会把预发布版本排除在外，所以只写 `<0.3.0` 会悄悄丢掉所有 `0.2.2-*` 构建，alpha 与 rc 都一样。两个子句都止于 `0.3.0`，下一条线因此是一个单独的决定，而不是悄悄放宽。

可选的 `@deepseek-ai/cordis` peer 跟随 typert 的范围。每条线都推进了宿主内核：`0.2.1` 的构建依赖 `~4.0.5`（或 `4.0.5` 的预发布版本），`0.2.2` 的 alpha 依赖 `4.0.6` 的预发布版本，`0.2.2-rc.1` 依赖 `~4.1.0`。全新安装会采用**最新**被接纳的 typert 构建所依赖的那个 cordis，所以 cordis peer 漏掉它就会以 `ERESOLVE` 失败；漏掉较早某条线的 cordis，则会在已安装该线宿主的环境旁安装失败。因此这个 peer 接纳其中每一个，并止于下一个版本元组：

```
~4.0.4 || >=4.0.5-0 <4.1.0 || >=4.0.6-0 <4.1.0 || ~4.1.0
```

| 层面 | 目标 |
| :-- | :-- |
| **Harness 版本线** | **`0.2.1`** 与 **`0.2.2`** 预发布版本，`alpha` 与 `rc` 通道均可（peer：见上方范围） |
| **宿主内核** | `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 从 `4.0.4` 到 `4.1.x`，包括 `4.0.5` 与 `4.0.6` 的预发布版本（可选 peer：见上方范围） |
| **插件包** | [`dsh-opencode-patch`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencode-patch) |
| **宿主 profile** | DSH Web profile（`patchReload: live`） |
| **声明的路由** | `opencode`、`opencode-go`、`opencode-responses`、`opencode-anthropic` |
| **网关** | `opencode.ai/zen/v1`（`/responses`、`/chat/completions`、`/messages`、`:streamGenerateContent`）、`zen/go/v1`（`/chat/completions`） |
| **模型目录** | 由 `models.opencode.ai/api.json` 生成；下线判定直接跟随目录自身的 `status: "deprecated"` 标记，不维护任何手工 id 列表 |
| **上游 pi** | **不随包携带。** 桥接在运行时加载 harness 已安装的那份 `@earendil-works/pi-ai`，因此 harness 升级不会与本插件锁定的副本产生版本错位 |
| **验证关卡** | `vp check` 干净、确定性单元与离线网关 mock 套件全绿、完整 schema 校验、消费者安装 + 加载（[`scripts/check.ts`](./scripts/check.ts)） |
请求头注入矩阵、会话谱系、工作区归属、API 层级与目录内部实现，都在 **[docs/deep-dive.md](./docs/deep-dive.md)**。本 README 只讲你看得见的界面和要配的东西。

灵感来自 [@nobu121](https://github.com/nobu121) 的 [**`nobu121/dsh-opencode-session`**](https://github.com/nobu121/dsh-opencode-session)，该项目开创了 OpenCode on DSH 的会话 ID 处理。本插件由 [@viztor](https://github.com/viztor) **独立实现**：沿用了这个思路，其余部分都是重写的——Zen 免费层网关兼容、分层子代理谱系、动态工作区项目归属、实时双模式 Go 额度与 Zen 余额监控，以及原生 Web UI 集成。
